text: Morning, George — happy Sunday, the second of August.
Good news to open with: yesterday's extreme fire alert has eased a notch, so Attica's down from category five to category four today — still very high, but the water-bombing planes can fly again.
— personal items —
Abroad, the big one is on Europe's own doorstep.
More than sixty thousand migrants crossed from Morocco into Spain's little enclave of Ceuta in a single day, and the death toll has climbed to sixty-seven — it's completely overwhelmed the place.
Italy's reacted by suspending the Schengen open border with Spain and bringing back air and sea checks, which tells you how rattled European capitals are right now.
Meanwhile the war in Ukraine flared again over the weekend — Russian ballistic missiles hit Kyiv, killing at least nine people and wounding more than thirty.
A grim reminder the capital is still very much a target.

And from the science desk, something lovely: astronomers have spotted a second supernova wreck sitting right beside the famous Jellyfish Nebula, and the evidence says the two are siblings — a pair of stars that once orbited each other, then blew up separately, leaving twin graves side by side.
Over to AI, and the very top of the table hasn't budged — Claude's Opus 5 is still the smartest model going.
But the interesting move is at the cheap end: DeepSeek's just dropped a new Flash model that's absurdly inexpensive, pennies per million tokens, and quick with it.
If you're running anything at volume where you don't need the absolute frontier, it's worth a look.
Anything else claiming a big new flagship right now is rumour until it actually ships.
Weather at home: another hot, dry one — mid-twenties first thing, up around thirty this afternoon, clear skies and no rain.
The wind's lighter than yesterday's gale, a steady north-easterly, and the fire danger's down to very high rather than extreme.
Sun sets about half past eight.

One for the climbing world, and it's a sad one: Nirmal Purja — Nimsdai, the guy from Fourteen Peaks — has gone missing on Broad Peak in Pakistan after an avalanche swept him and several other climbers.
There's no confirmation either way yet, so fingers crossed, but it doesn't sound good.
— personal items —
With thirty degrees and dry air today, keep the water topped up all the way through — more than feels necessary.
And to send you off — word of the day is "heel hook": in climbing, hooking your heel over a hold and pulling with your leg like a third limb, as in "I heel-hooked the lip and rocked over the top."
And a quick AI tip: when a model's answer comes back wrong, don't just re-ask the same thing — tell it exactly what was off and let it retry; that feedback fixes it far better than a blank do-over.
— personal items —
Talk tomorrow.
